accessibility:
- The root `Navbar` renders as `<nav role="navigation" aria-label="main navigation">`.
  The default accessible name is `main navigation`. A screen reader announces it with
  the role, and since the name holds the role word, "navigation" is heard twice.
  Pass a name without the role word (`aria-label="Site"`), and a different name
  on each Navbar when a page has more than one. A passed `aria-label` replaces
  the default.
- `Navbar.Item active` sets `aria-current="page"` on the element `as` renders, the link by
  default, so the current item isn't only a color. An `aria-current` you pass wins: a navbar of
  sections on one page can say `"location"`, and `aria-current={false}` turns it off.
- Bulma fills an active link item with its selected color, the link color in a navbar with no
  `color`, and bestax's styles give its text the color Bulma picks to read on that fill,
  `--bulma-navbar-item-selected-color-l`. Bulma's own stylesheet leaves the text in the navbar's
  normal text color, dark gray on blue on the light scheme, so the rule ships in `bestax.css` and
  `extras.css`. A `--bulma-navbar-item-color` you set on the item itself still wins, and an item
  with a `bgColor` keeps the navbar's text color. A rule of your own that takes the fill off
  restates `color` too.
- Use semantic links (`<a>`) and buttons, and provide clear `aria-label` and `aria-expanded` for the burger toggle.
- `Navbar.Link` inside a `Navbar.Dropdown` automatically gets `aria-haspopup="true"` and
  `aria-expanded` synced to the dropdown's open state — no manual wiring required.
  <kbd>Enter</kbd>/<kbd>Space</kbd> toggle the dropdown open/closed, and <kbd>Escape</kbd>
  closes it and keeps focus on the link. <kbd>Escape</kbd> anywhere else in the open dropdown, its
  menu included, puts focus back on the link and closes it too, unless a control there marks the
  key used, the key comes from a dialog or from content opened from the menu into a portal, or
  focus can't go back to the link. When the trigger isn't interactive on its own — no
  `href`, not `as="button"`, and not a custom component — it also gets `role="button"` and
  `tabIndex={0}` so it's reachable and operable by keyboard, and a mouse/touch click on it
  toggles the dropdown too (a caller-supplied `onClick` still runs, and can
  `preventDefault()` to opt out).
- A custom component passed to `as` keeps its own semantics, because a router link takes `to`
  rather than `href` and so can't be recognised from the props it's given. If yours renders
  something non-interactive instead, pass `role="button"` and it takes the fallback above —
  `tabIndex` and click included. The keyboard path is wired either way.
- `hoverable` dropdowns keep working with a mouse (hover-to-open); the keyboard path above
  opens and closes them independently of hover. Bulma shows a `hoverable` dropdown's menu while
  the pointer is on it and while focus is in it, the link included, on a desktop-wide window.
  <kbd>Escape</kbd> puts a menu shown that way away, and it stays away until the pointer has left
  the dropdown and focus has too, or until the pointer comes back or focus moves onto something in
  it. From the page, the key goes on to what has focus; from inside
  the dropdown, focus moves to the link, with the same exceptions as for an open one, such as focus
  that can't go back to the link, where the menu stays. Below the desktop breakpoint, where the menu always
  shows under the burger, Escape doesn't put it away, though it still closes an open one.
- **Forced colors:** Bulma draws the burger's bars as a background color, which forced colors
  (Windows' contrast themes) replaces, so the burger would vanish there while it still works and
  takes focus. bestax's styles keep its bars visible in the system's button text color. That rule
  ships in `bestax.css` and `extras.css`, not in Bulma's own stylesheet, and an
  [`AppFrame`](https://bestax.io/docs/api/layout/appframe)'s burger gets it too. Bulma marks an active or selected
  link item, `Navbar.Link` and dropdown row with a fill and a text color alone, which forced
  colors replaces, so bestax's styles draw a bar in the system's highlight color inside it there:
  along its bottom in a row, and down its start edge where the items stack, in a dropdown and in
  the menu the burger opens. The item and everything in it stay in the contrast theme's colors,
  and an active tab gets the bar above Bulma's thicker underline. This ships in the same
  stylesheets.
- **`Navbar.Divider` in forced colors:** Bulma draws it as a background color too, which forced
  colors paints in the dropdown's own color, so the line would vanish. bestax's styles draw it in
  the system's text color there, from the same stylesheets.
- **In a colored [`Hero`](https://bestax.io/docs/api/layout/hero):** Bulma's hero sets the colors its navbar's items
  take on hover and when active, but Bulma's navbar doesn't read them, so a focused or hovered
  item took the scheme's fill under the hero's text, and the active item and the burger took the
  link color. For a `Navbar` with no `color` of its own, bestax's styles draw a focused, hovered or
  active item in the hero's text color with the hero's background color as its text, the burger
  and a tab in the hero's text color, and the dropdown arrow in its link's text color. The menu the
  burger opens, and the dropdown's rows in it, take the hero's background and text, except an
  active row, which keeps Bulma's selected fill and the text that reads on it, and on a phone a bold hero's menu takes the hero's
  own gradient. Where `Navbar.DropdownMenu` is a box of its own, on a desktop, its links keep
  Bulma's colors. That rule ships in `bestax.css` and `extras.css`, not in Bulma's own stylesheet.

:::note
There's no arrow-key roving between navbar items and no outside-click handling for
`Navbar.Dropdown` — Bulma navbar dropdowns are hover/click surfaces, so this is intentionally
kept simple.
:::

parts.summary: The `Navbar` component implements Bulma's powerful, responsive navigation bar for your Bulma React UI.

props.name: className
props.description: Additional CSS classes for the navbar.

props.name: color
props.description: Bulma color modifier for the navbar.

props.name: transparent
props.description: Renders the navbar with a transparent background.

props.name: isSpaced
props.description: Renders Bulma's `is-spaced`: padding around the navbar, rounded items and boxed dropdowns. Bulma applies it from the desktop breakpoint up, so below that the navbar looks the same either way. With `fixed="top"`, put `has-spaced-navbar-fixed-top` on `<html>` beside `has-navbar-fixed-top` (the `-bottom` pair for `fixed="bottom"`). From desktop up the spaced navbar is taller than `has-navbar-fixed-top` pads the page for, and there the spaced class pads it for the taller navbar.

props.name: hasShadow
props.description: Renders Bulma's `has-shadow`: a shadow below the navbar, or above it with `fixed="bottom"`. Off unless set, since Bulma's navbar has no shadow of its own. `Box` and `Card` take a `hasShadow` that defaults to `true` instead, because Bulma gives those a shadow already.

props.name: fixed
props.description: Fixes the navbar to the top or bottom of the viewport.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Accessible name. Defaults to `main navigation`. A screen reader announces it with the landmark's role, and since the name holds the role word, "navigation" is heard twice. Pass a name without it (`aria-label="Site"`), and a different name on each Navbar when a page has more than one. A passed `aria-label` replaces the default, and `aria-label={undefined}` removes it, leaving the landmark unnamed.

extraProps.name: ref
extraProps.description: Ref forwarded to the root `<nav>` element.

parts.summary: Navigation links, buttons, or custom content

props.name: as
props.description: Render as another intrinsic element (`'span'`, `'div'`, `'button'`) or a custom component (e.g. a router link). Defaults to `'a'`. `'button'` renders `type="button"`, so an item inside a form does not submit it. Pass `type="submit"` or `type="reset"` and yours is used; any other value, or a spread carrying `type: undefined`, renders `type="button"`.

props.name: active
props.description: Marks the item as the current one. It adds Bulma's `is-active` class, and `aria-current="page"` on the element `as` renders, so assistive tech can tell which item is current too. An `aria-current` you pass wins, even `undefined`: use it to say something else (`"location"` for a section of one page, say), or `aria-current={false}` to turn it off. An `active` item that isn't navigation takes `aria-current={false}`: an `as="button"` control, say, or a `has-dropdown` container like the `<Navbar.Item as="div" className="has-dropdown" active>` older bestax-migrate versions wrote. That one can be a `Navbar.Dropdown` instead. Bulma fills an active link item with its selected color, the link color in a navbar with no `color`. bestax's stylesheets give the text that color's invert, where Bulma's own leaves it in the navbar's text color, dark gray on blue on the light scheme. With a `bgColor` the text keeps the navbar's color, and a fill of your own from CSS wants a `textColor` too.

extraProps.name: ref
extraProps.description: Ref forwarded to the element `as` renders, typed from `as`: the DOM node for an intrinsic tag, or whatever handle a custom component exposes.

parts.summary: Dropdown trigger with arrow indicator (use as first child of `Navbar.Dropdown`)

props.name: as
props.description: Render as another intrinsic element (`'button'`, `'span'`) or a custom component. Defaults to `'a'`. Inside a `Navbar.Dropdown` this also decides the trigger's semantics. A custom component is taken to be interactive already — a router link, typically — so it keeps its own role and click behaviour. An intrinsic tag is judged on what it is: `'button'`, or anything carrying an `href`, is left alone, and everything else (`'span'`, a bare `'a'`, a custom element) gets `role="button"`, `tabIndex` and a click that opens the dropdown. If your custom component renders something non-interactive, pass `role="button"` and it takes that fallback too — `tabIndex` and click included. The keyboard path is attached either way. `'button'` renders `type="button"`, so a link inside a form does not submit it. Pass `type="submit"` or `type="reset"` and yours is used; any other value, or a spread carrying `type: undefined`, renders `type="button"`.

extraProps.name: ref
extraProps.description: Ref forwarded to the element `as` renders, typed from `as`: the DOM node for an intrinsic tag, or whatever handle a custom component exposes.

parts.catchAll: Remaining props of the element or component selected by as (default <a>) and Bulma helper props

props.name: color
props.description: Renders `has-text-<color>`, exactly like `textColor`. Bulma has no `.navbar-burger.is-<color>` rule, so this is not a filled variant. `textColor` takes precedence when both are set, and is the one that reaches the full color list.

props.name: children
props.description: Custom content inside the burger, rendered after its four bar spans. Bulma styles every `<span>` in the burger as a bar, so an extra span here draws an extra bar.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Accessible name. Pass your own to replace it. An empty one, or a spread carrying `'aria-label': undefined`, keeps the default rather than leaving the button unnamed.

props.name: aria-expanded
props.description: Expanded state for assistive technology. It follows `active` unless you pass `true` or `false`, and `null` leaves it off, for a burger whose state isn't known yet; a spread carrying `'aria-expanded': undefined` still follows `active`.

extraProps.name: ref
extraProps.description: Ref forwarded to the burger button element.

extraProps.name: type
extraProps.description: Button type. Defaults to `'button'`, so a burger inside a form does not submit it. Pass `'submit'` or `'reset'` and yours is used; any other value, or a spread carrying `type: undefined`, renders `'button'`.

parts.summary: Dropdown parent (with options for hover, up, right, active)

props.name: hoverable
props.description: Dropdown opens on hover, and while focus is in it, as Bulma's navbar shows it on a desktop-wide window. Escape puts away a menu the pointer or focus is showing there, and it stays away until the pointer has left the dropdown and focus has too, or until the pointer comes back or focus moves onto something in it. Escape from inside the dropdown puts focus on its `Navbar.Link` first, and leaves the menu as it is in the cases `active` lists, such as when focus can't go back to the link.

props.name: active
props.description: Dropdown is open, whether you control it or not. Escape on its `Navbar.Link`, or anywhere else in the open dropdown, closes it and puts focus on the link, unless a control there marks the key used, the key comes from a dialog or from content opened from the menu into a portal, or focus can't go back to the link.

props.name: onActiveChange
props.description: Callback when dropdown active state changes.
